name: The Ritz Carlton Mexico City
positioning: Contemporary luxury hotel on Paseo de la Reforma overlooking Chapultepec Park (official name The Ritz-Carlton, Mexico City), with a rooftop bar and a spa inspired by Aztec traditions
best_for: Travelers who want a Reforma base overlooking Chapultepec Park
Guests who enjoy art, design and hands-on Mexican culinary experiences

facts.text: The hotel overlooks Chapultepec Park in the Reforma area of Mexico City.
The address is Avenida Paseo de la Reforma 509, Cuauhtemoc, Mexico City.
The hotel's design draws on surrealism, ancient rituals, folklore and the energy of contemporary Mexico.
Mexican artist Emilio Chapela created original works for selected rooms and suites.
Samos is the hotel restaurant, serving Mexican cuisine reimagined with a contemporary approach and local, seasonal ingredients.
Carlotta is the hotel's rooftop cocktail bar.
The spa has a steam room and a sauna.
The hotel has an indoor pool.
The Polanco district, with designer shops and high-end dining, is practically next door.
Toronto firm Chapi Chapo Design gave the hotel a streamlined look with clean geometries and floor-to-ceiling windows.

highlights.text: Most rooms have private balconies with panoramic views over Chapultepec forest.
Multimedia artist Omar Barquet created site-specific works for the elevator halls.
Spa treatments use botanical ingredients combined with the healing and spiritual traditions of Mexico City's Aztec culture.
A Xochimilco experience led by agroecology expert Lucio Usobiaga includes a ride on a traditional trajinera boat.
Guests can take a cooking class on making Mexican mole and hand-pressed tortillas with Chef Nayelli Caballero.

considerations.text: The thick glass panels at the balconies magnify the afternoon sun and block mountain breezes, making the balconies hard to use through much of the day.
The hotel does not provide shuttle service.
Club access needs an upgraded booking; Marriott Bonvoy elite status does not give complimentary Club access.
